observations: First argument is 32-bit display number; second and third arguments are pointers to 32-bit outputs, cleared at entry
get_canonical_display_id runs before display lookup; do not mistake its result for CGS connection ID
WindowServer request ID 0x84d5, reply ID 0x8539; 40-byte request, complex 52-byte success reply with one port descriptor and one trailing 32-bit field
Actual unsupported/no-display path returns CGError 1000 with zeroed outputs
CoreDisplay server path confirms the second output is an accelerator service port and the third is the IOAccelFindAccelerator framebuffer index; exact original byte ranges are pinned below.
scope: Darling CoreGraphics client-side accelerator query via actual CGDisplayIOServicePort and IOAccelFindAccelerator. Borrowed cached output and failure cleanup. Real graphics devices, mirror/hotplug behavior and hardware acceleration are not established by selected tests.
native_cached_output_semantics: CoreDisplay IOAccelFindAccelerator call stores port at MPPriv+0x5c and framebuffer index at +0x98 (0x7ff805408b95); MPAcceleratorForDisplayDevice returns these exact two fields (0x7ff8053f4adf and 0x7ff8053f4aea). SkyLight caches the send right and returns it without retaining.
